does: Cooks rice by coating it in hot fat with sweated onion, then letting it absorb a measured amount of hot stock under a lid.

intro.what: Rice is coated in fat, then absorbs hot stock without stirring beneath a close lid.
intro.why: Coating and controlled absorption produce separate grains. Resting and gentle fluffing complete the texture without stirring it into creaminess.

how: Sweat finely cut onion in butter without colour.
Stir in the rice until every grain is coated and turns glassy at the edges.
Pour in the hot stock all at once, add a bouquet garni and bring to a boil.
Cover closely with paper and a lid, and finish in the oven or over the lowest heat, without stirring.
Rest it off the heat, then fluff it with a fork and a little butter.

cues.text: The grains are separate and dry, with small steam holes across the surface and no liquid left.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring or lifting the lid while it cooks, which breaks the grains and lets the steam out.
mistakes.fix: Leave it shut until the time is up.
Measure the rice by volume and the stock against it. With too much, it turns to porridge.

quiz.question: What texture is this pilaf method intended to produce?
choices: Distinct grains rather than a creamy mass.
quiz.because: The method limits disturbance so the grains retain their separate shape.

quiz.question: When is the hot stock added?
choices: Before the onion has softened or rice is coated.
Only after the rice has finished resting.
After the rice is coated in fat.
quiz.because: Coating comes before covered absorption in this sequence.

quiz.question: Which surface appearance fits the intended result?
choices: Steam holes and no remaining loose liquid.
A deep pool above the grains.
A stirred glossy paste without distinct grains.
quiz.because: Steam holes and absorbed liquid accompany the separate-grain texture.

quiz.question: The pilaf became porridge after the stock was guessed. What would you change next time?
choices: Add stock without regard to the rice.
Measure the liquid against the rice.
Stir continuously to distribute the extra liquid.
quiz.because: Controlling the liquid helps avoid more moisture than the rice can absorb into the intended texture.

comes_after.why: A pilaf begins by sweating onion.
